stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the orange weight $P_2$ along the bar. Watch the moments panel: $M_1 = P_1 \cdot d_1$ pulls counter-clockwise, $M_2 = P_2 \cdot d_2$ pulls clockwise. The bar settles horizontal when they cancel.
stages.concept: Theorem of moments about a fixed axis: a solid free to rotate around $\Delta$ is in equilibrium when the algebraic sum of external moments vanishes — $\sum M_\Delta(\vec F_{ext}) = 0$. For two weights hanging on either side of the pivot, this reduces to $P_1 \cdot d_1 = P_2 \cdot d_2$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Three scenarios. Each fixes $P_1$, $d_1$, and $P_2$ — you set $d_2$ so the bar balances. Drag $P_2$, then press Confirm (or Space). You have 5 attempts to solve all 3.
stages.concept: For each scenario, apply $P_1 \cdot d_1 = P_2 \cdot d_2$ and solve for the unknown lever arm: $d_2 = \dfrac{P_1 \cdot d_1}{P_2}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The moments panel is off. The bar no longer tilts to guide you. Read $P_1$, $d_1$, and $P_2$ from the labels, compute $d_2$ on paper, drag $P_2$ to that position, then Confirm. One shot per scenario.
stages.concept: Blind application of the moment theorem: $d_2 = \dfrac{P_1 \cdot d_1}{P_2}$. Sign matters — if $P_2$ sits on the same side of $\Delta$ as $P_1$, both moments push the same way and the bar cannot balance.

labels.exhausted: OUT OF ATTEMPTS · RESET TO RETRY
labels.tip3: compute d2, set it, then confirm

1.1: Grab the orange weight and drag it along the bar. The bar tilts toward whichever moment wins.
1.2: Two moments act on the bar: $M_1$ from $P_1$ (counter-clockwise, positive) and $M_2$ from $P_2$ (clockwise, negative when $P_2$ is right of the pivot).
1.3: Equilibrium happens when $M_1 + M_2 = 0$, i.e. $P_1 \cdot d_1 = P_2 \cdot d_2$. Try to slide $P_2$ until the moments panel reads $\Sigma M \approx 0$.

2.1: Read $P_1$, $d_1$ and $P_2$ from the on-bar labels for the current scenario.
2.2: Compute the target $d_2 = P_1 \cdot d_1 / P_2$. Example: $P_1 = 4$ N, $d_1 = 15$ cm, $P_2 = 6$ N gives $d_2 = 10$ cm.
2.3: Drag $P_2$ so the live d2 readout in the top-right matches your computed value, then press Confirm. Budget is 5 attempts for 3 scenarios.

3.1: The tilt is frozen — you can no longer eyeball equilibrium. Do the arithmetic on paper first.
3.2: $d_2 = P_1 \cdot d_1 / P_2$. The current $d_2$ appears in the top-right corner as you drag.
3.3: Peek surfaces the theorem plus your current $d_2$ — verify your paper answer, then Confirm. One shot per scenario.
